     6	import Mathlib.AlgebraicGeometry.Gluing
     7	import Mathlib.AlgebraicGeometry.Pullbacks
     8	
     9	/-!
    10	# Gluing affine schemes from ring maps
    11	
    12	This file packages affine ring data into `Scheme.GlueData`.  The overlap restriction
    13	maps are the algebra maps `A i -> B i j`.  Thus an application with specified restriction
    14	maps should install the corresponding `Algebra (A i) (B i j)` structures (for example via
    15	`r.toRingHom.toAlgebra`) before invoking the constructor.
    16	
    17	The only non-formal coherence assumptions are ring identities:
    18	
    19	* each transition `tau i j : B j i -> B i j` is the identity on the diagonal;
    20	* the triple transition `theta i j k` sends the right tensor inclusion to the left
    21	  inclusion followed by `tau i j`;
    22	* the three cyclic triple transitions compose to the identity.
    23	
    24	The constructor conjugates `Spec.map theta` by Mathlib's `pullbackSpecIso`.  The face and
    25	cocycle fields of `Scheme.GlueData` are then discharged from the displayed ring identities.
    26	-/
    27	
    28	set_option autoImplicit false
    29	
    30	universe u
    31	
    32	open CategoryTheory Limits AlgebraicGeometry
    33	open scoped TensorProduct
    34	
    35	namespace AlgebraicJacobian
    36	
    37	noncomputable section
    38	
    39	variable {R J : Type u} [CommRing R]
    40	variable (A : J → Type u) (B : J → J → Type u)
    41	variable [∀ i, CommRing (A i)] [∀ i j, CommRing (B i j)]
    42	variable [∀ i, Algebra R (A i)] [∀ i j, Algebra R (B i j)]
    43	variable [∀ i j, Algebra (A i) (B i j)]
    44	variable [∀ i j, IsScalarTower R (A i) (B i j)]
    45	
    46	/-- The coordinate ring of the pullback of the two overlaps based at chart `i`. -/
    47	abbrev AffineTripleTensor (i j k : J) : Type u :=
    48	  B i j ⊗[A i] B i k
    49	
    50	/-- The left overlap inclusion into an affine triple tensor, viewed over `R`. -/
    51	def affineTensorIncludeLeft (i j k : J) :
    52	    B i j →ₐ[R] AffineTripleTensor A B i j k :=
    53	  (Algebra.TensorProduct.includeLeft :
    54	    B i j →ₐ[A i] B i j ⊗[A i] B i k).restrictScalars R
    55	
    56	/-- The right overlap inclusion into an affine triple tensor, viewed over `R`. -/
    57	def affineTensorIncludeRight (i j k : J) :
    58	    B i k →ₐ[R] AffineTripleTensor A B i j k :=
    59	  (Algebra.TensorProduct.includeRight :
    60	    B i k →ₐ[A i] B i j ⊗[A i] B i k).restrictScalars R
    61	
    62	/-- The affine overlap inclusion induced contravariantly by `A i -> B i j`. -/
    63	abbrev affineRestriction (i j : J) :
    64	    Spec (CommRingCat.of (B i j)) ⟶ Spec (CommRingCat.of (A i)) :=
    65	  Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap (A i) (B i j)))
    66	
    67	/-- The affine transition induced contravariantly by `tau i j : B j i -> B i j`. -/
    68	abbrev affineTransition (tau : ∀ i j, B j i →ₐ[R] B i j) (i j : J) :
    69	    Spec (CommRingCat.of (B i j)) ⟶ Spec (CommRingCat.of (B j i)) :=
    70	  Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (tau i j).toRingHom)
    71	
    72	/-- The canonical affine chart for a triple pullback. -/
    73	abbrev affineTriplePullbackIso (i j k : J) :
    74	    pullback (affineRestriction A B i j) (affineRestriction A B i k) ≅
    75	      Spec (CommRingCat.of (AffineTripleTensor A B i j k)) :=
    76	  pullbackSpecIso (A i) (B i j) (B i k)
    77	
    78	/-- A ring map between the rotated triple tensor rings, conjugated into a morphism between
    79	the actual scheme pullbacks used by `Scheme.GlueData`. -/
    80	def affineTripleTransition
    81	    (theta : ∀ i j k,
    82	      AffineTripleTensor A B j k i →ₐ[R] AffineTripleTensor A B i j k)
    83	    (i j k : J) :
    84	    pullback (affineRestriction A B i j) (affineRestriction A B i k) ⟶
    85	      pullback (affineRestriction A B j k) (affineRestriction A B j i) :=
    86	  (affineTriplePullbackIso A B i j k).hom ≫
    87	    Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (theta i j k).toRingHom) ≫
    88	      (affineTriplePullbackIso A B j k i).inv
    89	
    90	variable (tau : ∀ i j, B j i →ₐ[R] B i j)
    91	variable (theta : ∀ i j k,
    92	  AffineTripleTensor A B j k i →ₐ[R] AffineTripleTensor A B i j k)
    93	
    94	/-- The right-face ring identity implies the factorization field of `Scheme.GlueData`. -/
    95	@[reassoc]
    96	theorem affineTripleTransition_fac
    97	    (hfac : ∀ i j k,
    98	      (theta i j k).comp (affineTensorIncludeRight A B j k i) =
    99	        (affineTensorIncludeLeft A B i j k).comp (tau i j))
   100	    (i j k : J) :
   101	    affineTripleTransition A B theta i j k ≫
   102	        pullback.snd (affineRestriction A B j k) (affineRestriction A B j i) =
   103	      pullback.fst (affineRestriction A B i j) (affineRestriction A B i k) ≫
   104	        affineTransition B tau i j := by
   105	  have hfac' :
   106	      CommRingCat.ofHom
   107	          (((theta i j k).comp (affineTensorIncludeRight A B j k i)).toRingHom) =
   108	        CommRingCat.ofHom
   109	          (((affineTensorIncludeLeft A B i j k).comp (tau i j)).toRingHom) :=
   110	    congrArg (fun f => CommRingCat.ofHom f.toRingHom) (hfac i j k)
   111	  simp only [affineTripleTransition, Category.assoc]
   112	  rw [pullbackSpecIso_inv_snd]
   113	  rw [← Spec.map_comp, ← CommRingCat.ofHom_comp]
   114	  change (pullbackSpecIso (A i) (B i j) (B i k)).hom ≫
   115	      Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom
   116	        (((theta i j k).comp
   117	          (affineTensorIncludeRight A B j k i)).toRingHom)) =
   118	      pullback.fst (affineRestriction A B i j) (affineRestriction A B i k) ≫
   119	        affineTransition B tau i j
   120	  rw [hfac']
   121	  rw [show
   122	      ((affineTensorIncludeLeft A B i j k).comp (tau i j)).toRingHom =
   123	        (affineTensorIncludeLeft A B i j k).toRingHom.comp
   124	          (tau i j).toRingHom by rfl]
   125	  rw [CommRingCat.ofHom_comp, Spec.map_comp]
   126	  change (pullbackSpecIso (A i) (B i j) (B i k)).hom ≫
   127	      Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom
   128	        (Algebra.TensorProduct.includeLeftRingHom :
   129	          B i j →+* AffineTripleTensor A B i j k)) ≫
   130	      Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (tau i j).toRingHom) =
   131	      pullback.fst (affineRestriction A B i j) (affineRestriction A B i k) ≫
   132	        affineTransition B tau i j
   133	  rw [← Category.assoc, pullbackSpecIso_hom_fst]
   134	
   135	/-- A cyclic identity of triple-tensor ring maps implies the scheme-level cocycle. -/
   136	theorem affineTripleTransition_cocycle
   137	    (hcycle : ∀ i j k,
   138	      (theta i j k).comp ((theta j k i).comp (theta k i j)) =
   139	        AlgHom.id R (AffineTripleTensor A B i j k))
   140	    (i j k : J) :
   141	    affineTripleTransition A B theta i j k ≫
   142	        affineTripleTransition A B theta j k i ≫
   143	          affineTripleTransition A B theta k i j =
   144	      𝟙 (pullback (affineRestriction A B i j) (affineRestriction A B i k)) := by
   145	  have hmap :
   146	      Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (theta i j k).toRingHom) ≫
   147	          Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (theta j k i).toRingHom) ≫
   148	            Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (theta k i j).toRingHom) =
   149	        𝟙 (Spec (CommRingCat.of (AffineTripleTensor A B i j k))) := by
   150	    rw [← Spec.map_comp, ← CommRingCat.ofHom_comp]
   151	    rw [← Spec.map_comp, ← CommRingCat.ofHom_comp]
   152	    have hcycle' :
   153	        CommRingCat.ofHom
   154	            (((theta i j k).comp
   155	              ((theta j k i).comp (theta k i j))).toRingHom) =
   156	          CommRingCat.ofHom
   157	            ((AlgHom.id R (AffineTripleTensor A B i j k)).toRingHom) :=
   158	      congrArg (fun f => CommRingCat.ofHom f.toRingHom) (hcycle i j k)
   159	    change Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom
   160	      (((theta i j k).comp
   161	        ((theta j k i).comp (theta k i j))).toRingHom)) =
   162	      𝟙 (Spec (CommRingCat.of (AffineTripleTensor A B i j k)))
   163	    rw [hcycle']
   164	    rw [show (AlgHom.id R (AffineTripleTensor A B i j k)).toRingHom =
   165	      RingHom.id (AffineTripleTensor A B i j k) by rfl]
   166	    rw [CommRingCat.ofHom_id, Spec.map_id]
   167	  simp only [affineTripleTransition, Category.assoc, Iso.inv_hom_id_assoc]
   168	  rw [reassoc_of% hmap]
   169	  exact Iso.hom_inv_id _
   170	
   171	/-- A diagonal identity of overlap ring maps gives the diagonal transition identity. -/
   172	theorem affineTransition_self
   173	    (htau : ∀ i, tau i i = AlgHom.id R (B i i)) (i : J) :
   174	    affineTransition B tau i i = 𝟙 (Spec (CommRingCat.of (B i i))) := by
   175	  change Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (tau i i).toRingHom) = _
   176	  rw [htau]
   177	  rw [show (AlgHom.id R (B i i)).toRingHom = RingHom.id (B i i) by rfl]
   178	  rw [CommRingCat.ofHom_id, Spec.map_id]
   179	
   180	/-- Construct `Scheme.GlueData` from affine ring charts, overlap maps, and algebraic
   181	transition coherences.  Openness and the diagonal isomorphism remain geometric assumptions;
   182	the transition identity, factorization, and cocycle are discharged from ring equations. -/
   183	def affineRingGlueData
   184	    (tau : ∀ i j, B j i →ₐ[R] B i j)
   185	    (theta : ∀ i j k,
   186	      AffineTripleTensor A B j k i →ₐ[R] AffineTripleTensor A B i j k)
   187	    (fId : ∀ i, IsIso (affineRestriction A B i i))
   188	    (fOpen : ∀ i j, IsOpenImmersion (affineRestriction A B i j))
   189	    (tauId : ∀ i, tau i i = AlgHom.id R (B i i))
   190	    (thetaFac : ∀ i j k,
   191	      (theta i j k).comp (affineTensorIncludeRight A B j k i) =
   192	        (affineTensorIncludeLeft A B i j k).comp (tau i j))
   193	    (thetaCocycle : ∀ i j k,
   194	      (theta i j k).comp ((theta j k i).comp (theta k i j)) =
   195	        AlgHom.id R (AffineTripleTensor A B i j k)) :
   196	    Scheme.GlueData.{u} := by
   197	  letI (i j : J) : IsOpenImmersion (affineRestriction A B i j) := fOpen i j
   198	  exact
   199	    { J := J
   200	      U := fun i => Spec (CommRingCat.of (A i))
   201	      V := fun p => Spec (CommRingCat.of (B p.1 p.2))
   202	      f := affineRestriction A B
   203	      f_id := fId
   204	      f_open := fOpen
   205	      t := affineTransition B tau
   206	      t_id := affineTransition_self B tau tauId
   207	      t' := affineTripleTransition A B theta
   208	      t_fac := affineTripleTransition_fac A B tau theta thetaFac
   209	      cocycle := affineTripleTransition_cocycle A B theta thetaCocycle }
   210	
   211	end
   212	
   213	end AlgebraicJacobian

     8	/-!
     9	# Canonical cocycles of representability isomorphisms
    10	
    11	`Functor.RepresentableBy.uniqueUpToIso` is defined by Yoneda uniqueness, but mathlib does
    12	not expose the two equations that descent data consume: its universal-element intertwining
    13	formula and transitivity for three independently chosen representing objects.  These generic
    14	lemmas make those equations explicit.  In particular, the transitivity theorem proves a
    15	three-face cocycle without defining the `1,3` face as a composite.
    16	-/
    17	
    18	set_option autoImplicit false
    19	
    20	universe v u u'
    21	
    22	open CategoryTheory
    23	
    24	namespace CategoryTheory.Functor.RepresentableBy
    25	
    26	/-- Transport a representation through the right adjoint of an adjunction.
    27	
    28	This is the categorical pullback step used for overlap bases: if `L ⊣ R`, then a
    29	representation of `F` by `Y` induces one of `L.op ⋙ F` by `R.obj Y`.  The statement
    30	requires only the adjunction; for schemes, `Over.mapPullbackAdj` supplies it whenever
    31	the relevant pullbacks exist, including tensor-product (non-field) bases. -/
    32	noncomputable def ofLeftAdjoint
    33	    {C : Type u} {D : Type u'} [Category.{v, u} C] [Category.{v, u'} D]
    34	    {L : C ⥤ D} {R : D ⥤ C} (adj : L ⊣ R)
    35	    {F : Dᵒᵖ ⥤ Type v} {Y : D} (e : F.RepresentableBy Y) :
    36	    (L.op ⋙ F).RepresentableBy (R.obj Y) :=
    37	  (adj.representableBy Y).ofIso (Functor.isoWhiskerLeft L.op e.toIso)
    38	
    39	/-- The universal element of `ofLeftAdjoint` is obtained by applying the adjunction inverse. -/
    40	theorem ofLeftAdjoint_homEquiv
    41	    {C : Type u} {D : Type u'} [Category.{v, u} C] [Category.{v, u'} D]
    42	    {L : C ⥤ D} {R : D ⥤ C} (adj : L ⊣ R)
    43	    {F : Dᵒᵖ ⥤ Type v} {Y : D} (e : F.RepresentableBy Y)
    44	    {X : C} (g : X ⟶ R.obj Y) :
    45	    (ofLeftAdjoint adj e).homEquiv g = e.homEquiv ((adj.homEquiv X Y).symm g) := by
    46	  rfl
    47	
    48	/-- Compare representations of two isomorphic presheaves.
    49	
    50	The source representation is first transported along `η`; the comparison is then the ordinary
    51	Yoneda comparison.  This is the canonical overlap isomorphism once the two pullback Picard
    52	presheaves have been identified. -/
    53	noncomputable def uniqueUpToIsoOfIso
    54	    {C : Type u} [Category.{v, u} C]
    55	    {F F' : Cᵒᵖ ⥤ Type v} {Y Y' : C}
    56	    (e : F.RepresentableBy Y) (e' : F'.RepresentableBy Y') (η : F ≅ F') : Y ≅ Y' :=
    57	  (e.ofIso η).uniqueUpToIso e'
    58	
    59	/-- The comparison in `uniqueUpToIsoOfIso` intertwines the two universal elements. -/
    60	theorem homEquiv_uniqueUpToIsoOfIso_hom
    61	    {C : Type u} [Category.{v, u} C]
    62	    {F F' : Cᵒᵖ ⥤ Type v} {Y Y' : C}
    63	    (e : F.RepresentableBy Y) (e' : F'.RepresentableBy Y') (η : F ≅ F')
    64	    {X : C} (f : X ⟶ Y) :
    65	    e'.homEquiv (f ≫ (uniqueUpToIsoOfIso e e' η).hom) =
    66	      η.hom.app (Opposite.op X) (e.homEquiv f) := by
    67	  change e'.homEquiv (f ≫ ((e.ofIso η).uniqueUpToIso e').hom) =
    68	    (e.ofIso η).homEquiv f
    69	  have h : ((e.ofIso η).uniqueUpToIso e').hom =
    70	      e'.homEquiv.symm ((e.ofIso η).homEquiv (𝟙 Y)) := rfl
    71	  rw [h, comp_homEquiv_symm, Equiv.apply_symm_apply]
    72	  rw [← (e.ofIso η).homEquiv_comp f (𝟙 Y), Category.comp_id]
    73	
    74	/-- Transporting a representation across conjugate adjunctions produces the conjugate
    75	right-adjoint isomorphism on the representing object. -/
    76	theorem uniqueUpToIsoOfIso_ofLeftAdjoint_conjugate
    77	    {C : Type u} {D : Type u'} [Category.{v, u} C] [Category.{v, u'} D]
    78	    {L₁ L₂ : C ⥤ D} {R₁ R₂ : D ⥤ C}
    79	    (adj₁ : L₁ ⊣ R₁) (adj₂ : L₂ ⊣ R₂) (α : L₂ ≅ L₁)
    80	    {F : Dᵒᵖ ⥤ Type v} {Y : D} (e : F.RepresentableBy Y) :
    81	    uniqueUpToIsoOfIso
    82	      (ofLeftAdjoint adj₁ e)
    83	      (ofLeftAdjoint adj₂ e)
    84	      (Functor.isoWhiskerRight (NatIso.op α) F) =
    85	      (conjugateIsoEquiv adj₁ adj₂ α).app Y := by
    86	  let e₁ := ofLeftAdjoint adj₁ e
    87	  let e₂ := ofLeftAdjoint adj₂ e
    88	  apply Iso.ext
    89	  apply e₂.homEquiv.injective
    90	  have h : (adj₂.homEquiv (R₁.obj Y) Y).symm
    91	      ((conjugateIsoEquiv adj₁ adj₂ α).app Y).hom =
    92	      α.hom.app (R₁.obj Y) ≫ adj₁.counit.app Y := by
    93	    apply (adj₂.homEquiv (R₁.obj Y) Y).injective
    94	    rw [Equiv.apply_symm_apply]
    95	    have hc := conjugateEquiv_counit adj₁ adj₂ α.hom Y
    96	    have hn := adj₂.homEquiv_naturality_left
    97	      (X' := R₁.obj Y) (X := R₂.obj Y) (Y := Y)
    98	      ((conjugateEquiv adj₁ adj₂ α.hom).app Y) (adj₂.counit.app Y)
    99	    have hunit : (adj₂.homEquiv (R₂.obj Y) Y) (adj₂.counit.app Y) =
   100	        𝟙 (R₂.obj Y) := by
   101	      have hh := adj₂.homEquiv_counit (R₂.obj Y) Y (𝟙 (R₂.obj Y))
   102	      have hh' := congrArg (adj₂.homEquiv (R₂.obj Y) Y) hh
   103	      simpa using hh'.symm
   104	    change (conjugateEquiv adj₁ adj₂ α.hom).app Y = _
   105	    calc
   106	      (conjugateEquiv adj₁ adj₂ α.hom).app Y =
   107	          (conjugateEquiv adj₁ adj₂ α.hom).app Y ≫ 𝟙 _ := by simp
   108	      _ = (conjugateEquiv adj₁ adj₂ α.hom).app Y ≫
   109	          (adj₂.homEquiv (R₂.obj Y) Y) (adj₂.counit.app Y) := by
   110	        rw [hunit, Category.comp_id]
   111	      _ = (adj₂.homEquiv (R₁.obj Y) Y)
   112	          (L₂.map ((conjugateEquiv adj₁ adj₂ α.hom).app Y) ≫ adj₂.counit.app Y) :=
   113	        hn.symm
   114	      _ = (adj₂.homEquiv (R₁.obj Y) Y)
   115	          (α.hom.app (R₁.obj Y) ≫ adj₁.counit.app Y) := by
   116	        exact congrArg (adj₂.homEquiv (R₁.obj Y) Y) hc
   117	  calc
   118	    e₂.homEquiv
   119	        (uniqueUpToIsoOfIso e₁ e₂
   120	          (Functor.isoWhiskerRight (NatIso.op α) F)).hom =
   121	      (Functor.isoWhiskerRight (NatIso.op α) F).hom.app
   122	          (Opposite.op (R₁.obj Y)) (e₁.homEquiv (𝟙 _)) := by
   123	      simpa using homEquiv_uniqueUpToIsoOfIso_hom
   124	        e₁ e₂ (Functor.isoWhiskerRight (NatIso.op α) F) (𝟙 _)
   125	    _ = e.homEquiv (α.hom.app (R₁.obj Y) ≫ adj₁.counit.app Y) := by
   126	      simp only [Functor.isoWhiskerRight_hom, Functor.whiskerRight_app]
   127	      dsimp [e₁]
   128	      rw [ofLeftAdjoint_homEquiv]
   129	      have hunit : (adj₁.homEquiv (R₁.obj Y) Y).symm (𝟙 (R₁.obj Y)) =
   130	          adj₁.counit.app Y := by
   131	        have hh := adj₁.homEquiv_counit (R₁.obj Y) Y (𝟙 (R₁.obj Y))
   132	        simpa using hh
   133	      rw [hunit]
   134	      change (ConcreteCategory.hom (F.map (α.hom.app (R₁.obj Y)).op))
   135	          (e.homEquiv (adj₁.counit.app Y)) =
   136	        e.homEquiv (α.hom.app (R₁.obj Y) ≫ adj₁.counit.app Y)
   137	      exact (e.homEquiv_comp
   138	        (α.hom.app (R₁.obj Y)) (adj₁.counit.app Y)).symm
   139	    _ = e₂.homEquiv ((conjugateIsoEquiv adj₁ adj₂ α).app Y).hom := by
   140	      rw [ofLeftAdjoint_homEquiv, h]
   141	      rfl

   143	/-- Applying one adjunction to two representations carries their canonical comparison
   144	to the image of the original comparison under the right adjoint. -/
   145	theorem uniqueUpToIsoOfIso_ofLeftAdjoint_mapIso
   146	    {C : Type u} {D : Type u'} [Category.{v, u} C] [Category.{v, u'} D]
   147	    {L : C ⥤ D} {R : D ⥤ C} (adj : L ⊣ R)
   148	    {F F' : Dᵒᵖ ⥤ Type v} {Y Y' : D}
   149	    (e : F.RepresentableBy Y) (e' : F'.RepresentableBy Y') (η : F ≅ F') :
   150	    uniqueUpToIsoOfIso
   151	      (ofLeftAdjoint adj e)
   152	      (ofLeftAdjoint adj e')
   153	      (Functor.isoWhiskerLeft L.op η) =
   154	      R.mapIso (uniqueUpToIsoOfIso e e' η) := by
   155	  apply Iso.ext
   156	  apply (ofLeftAdjoint adj e').homEquiv.injective
   157	  calc
   158	    (ofLeftAdjoint adj e').homEquiv
   159	        ((uniqueUpToIsoOfIso
   160	          (ofLeftAdjoint adj e)
   161	          (ofLeftAdjoint adj e')
   162	          (Functor.isoWhiskerLeft L.op η)).hom) =
   163	      (Functor.isoWhiskerLeft L.op η).hom.app
   164	        (Opposite.op (R.obj Y))
   165	        ((ofLeftAdjoint adj e).homEquiv (𝟙 _)) := by
   166	      simpa using homEquiv_uniqueUpToIsoOfIso_hom
   167	        (ofLeftAdjoint adj e)
   168	        (ofLeftAdjoint adj e')
   169	        (Functor.isoWhiskerLeft L.op η) (𝟙 _)
   170	    _ = (ofLeftAdjoint adj e').homEquiv
   171	        (R.mapIso (uniqueUpToIsoOfIso e e' η)).hom := by
   172	      change (ConcreteCategory.hom
   173	          (η.hom.app (L.op.obj (Opposite.op (R.obj Y)))))
   174	          (e.homEquiv ((adj.homEquiv (R.obj Y) Y).symm (𝟙 _))) =
   175	        e'.homEquiv ((adj.homEquiv (R.obj Y) Y').symm
   176	          (R.map (uniqueUpToIsoOfIso e e' η).hom))
   177	      rw [show (adj.homEquiv (R.obj Y) Y').symm
   178	          (R.map (uniqueUpToIsoOfIso e e' η).hom) =
   179	        (adj.homEquiv (R.obj Y) Y).symm (𝟙 _) ≫
   180	          (uniqueUpToIsoOfIso e e' η).hom by
   181	        simpa using adj.homEquiv_naturality_right_symm
   182	          (𝟙 (R.obj Y)) (uniqueUpToIsoOfIso e e' η).hom]
   183	      symm
   184	      exact homEquiv_uniqueUpToIsoOfIso_hom e e' η
   185	        ((adj.homEquiv (R.obj Y) Y).symm (𝟙 _))

   187	/-- The canonical comparison for the inverse presheaf isomorphism is the inverse
   188	of the original comparison. -/
   189	theorem uniqueUpToIsoOfIso_symm
   190	    {C : Type u} [Category.{v, u} C]
   191	    {F F' : Cᵒᵖ ⥤ Type v} {Y Y' : C}
   192	    (e : F.RepresentableBy Y) (e' : F'.RepresentableBy Y') (η : F ≅ F') :
   193	    (uniqueUpToIsoOfIso e e' η).symm =
   194	      uniqueUpToIsoOfIso e' e η.symm := by
   195	  let u := uniqueUpToIsoOfIso e e' η
   196	  let v := uniqueUpToIsoOfIso e' e η.symm
   197	  apply Iso.ext
   198	  change u.inv = v.hom
   199	  apply (cancel_mono u.hom).1
   200	  have hvu : v.hom ≫ u.hom = 𝟙 _ := by
   201	    apply e'.homEquiv.injective
   202	    calc
   203	      e'.homEquiv (v.hom ≫ u.hom) =
   204	          η.hom.app (Opposite.op Y')
   205	            (e.homEquiv v.hom) := by
   206	        simpa [u, v] using
   207	          homEquiv_uniqueUpToIsoOfIso_hom e e' η v.hom
   208	      _ = η.hom.app (Opposite.op Y')
   209	          (η.inv.app (Opposite.op Y') (e'.homEquiv (𝟙 _))) := by
   210	        rw [show e.homEquiv v.hom =
   211	            η.inv.app (Opposite.op Y') (e'.homEquiv (𝟙 _)) by
   212	          simpa [v] using
   213	            homEquiv_uniqueUpToIsoOfIso_hom e' e η.symm (𝟙 Y')]
   214	      _ = e'.homEquiv (𝟙 _) := by
   215	        have hh := η.inv_hom_id_app (Opposite.op Y')
   216	        exact congrArg (fun f => f (e'.homEquiv (𝟙 _))) hh
   217	  calc
   218	    u.inv ≫ u.hom = 𝟙 _ := u.inv_hom_id
   219	    _ = v.hom ≫ u.hom := hvu.symm

   221	/-- Transport through a composite adjunction is the same representation as transport
   222	through the two adjunctions successively. -/
   223	theorem ofLeftAdjoint_comp
   224	    {C : Type u} {D E : Type u'} [Category.{v, u} C]
   225	    [Category.{v, u'} D] [Category.{v, u'} E]
   226	    {L₁ : C ⥤ D} {R₁ : D ⥤ C} {L₂ : D ⥤ E} {R₂ : E ⥤ D}
   227	    (adj₁ : L₁ ⊣ R₁) (adj₂ : L₂ ⊣ R₂)
   228	    {F : Eᵒᵖ ⥤ Type v} {Y : E} (e : F.RepresentableBy Y) :
   229	    ofLeftAdjoint (adj₁.comp adj₂) e =
   230	      ofLeftAdjoint adj₁ (ofLeftAdjoint adj₂ e) := by
   231	  apply RepresentableBy.ext
   232	  change e.homEquiv
   233	      (((adj₁.comp adj₂).homEquiv ((R₂ ⋙ R₁).obj Y) Y).symm (𝟙 _)) =
   234	    e.homEquiv ((adj₂.homEquiv (L₁.obj ((R₂ ⋙ R₁).obj Y)) Y).symm
   235	      ((adj₁.homEquiv ((R₂ ⋙ R₁).obj Y) (R₂.obj Y)).symm (𝟙 _)))
   236	  rw [Adjunction.comp_homEquiv]
   237	  rfl

   240	/-- For over-categories, the canonical comparison between direct and iterated

    99	/-! ## The δ scheme system `S : (FinSubext k K)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Over (Spec k)` -/
   100	
   101	section SchemeSystem
   102	
   103	variable {k K : Type u} [Field k] [Field K] [Algebra k K]
   104	
   105	/-- The underlying scheme of `overSpec k A` is affine (it is `Spec A`). -/
   106	instance isAffine_overSpec_left (A : Type u) [CommRing A] [Algebra k A] :

   110	/-- The δ scheme transition morphism `Spec k''' ⟶ Spec k''` in `Over (Spec k)`, for
   111	`k'' ≤ k'''`: `Spec` of the field inclusion `k'' ↪ k'''`.  Well-defined over `Spec k`
   112	because the inclusion is a `k`-algebra map. -/
   113	noncomputable def deltaSchemeMap {L₁ L₂ : FinSubext k K} (h : L₁.1 ≤ L₂.1) :
   114	    overSpec k L₂.1 ⟶ overSpec k L₁.1 :=
   115	  Over.homMk (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (IntermediateField.inclusion h).toRingHom)) (by

   121	    (deltaSchemeMap h).left
   122	      = Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (IntermediateField.inclusion h).toRingHom) :=
   123	  rfl
   124	
   125	/-- **The δ scheme diagram.**  `S.obj (op k'') = overSpec k k'' = Spec k''` over `Spec k`,
   126	with the transition maps `Spec` of the field inclusions.  Its limit is `Spec K = overSpec k K`
   127	(`deltaSchemeIsLimit`). -/
   128	noncomputable def deltaSchemeDiagram : (FinSubext k K)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Over (Spec (.of k)) where
   129	  obj L := overSpec k (unop L).1
   130	  map {L₁ L₂} h := deltaSchemeMap (leOfHom h.unop)
   131	  map_id L := by
   132	    apply Over.OverMorphism.ext
   133	    simp only [deltaSchemeMap_left, Over.id_left, overSpec_left]
   134	    rw [← Spec.map_id]
   135	    congr 1
   136	  map_comp {L₁ L₂ L₃} f g := by
   137	    apply Over.OverMorphism.ext
   138	    simp only [Over.comp_left, deltaSchemeMap_left, overSpec_left, ← Spec.map_comp,
   139	      ← CommRingCat.ofHom_comp]
   140	    congr 2
   141	
   142	@[simp]
   143	lemma deltaSchemeDiagram_map {L₁ L₂ : (FinSubext k K)ᵒᵖ} (h : L₁ ⟶ L₂) :
   144	    deltaSchemeDiagram.map h = deltaSchemeMap (leOfHom h.unop) :=
   145	  rfl
   146	
   147	/-- Every δ transition map is affine (`Spec` of a field hom; both source and target are
   148	affine). -/
   149	instance deltaSchemeMap_isAffineHom {L₁ L₂ : FinSubext k K} (h : L₁.1 ≤ L₂.1) :
   150	    IsAffineHom (deltaSchemeMap h).left :=
   151	  isAffineHom_of_isAffine _
   152	
   153	/-- Every δ stage is a one-point (hence compact) space: `Spec` of a field. -/
   154	instance deltaSchemeDiagram_compactSpace (L : (FinSubext k K)ᵒᵖ) :
   155	    CompactSpace ((deltaSchemeDiagram.obj L).left) :=
   156	  inferInstanceAs (CompactSpace (Spec _))
   157	
   158	/-- Every δ stage is quasi-separated: `Spec` of a field is affine. -/
   159	instance deltaSchemeDiagram_quasiSeparatedSpace (L : (FinSubext k K)ᵒᵖ) :
   160	    QuasiSeparatedSpace ((deltaSchemeDiagram.obj L).left) :=
   161	  inferInstanceAs (QuasiSeparatedSpace (Spec _))
   162	
   163	end SchemeSystem

   165	/-! ## The δ scheme limit `Spec K = lim S` -/
   166	
   167	section SchemeLimit
   168	
   169	variable {k K : Type u} [Field k] [Field K] [Algebra k K] [Algebra.IsAlgebraic k K]
   170	
   171	/-- `Scheme.Spec` is a right adjoint (`Γ ⊣ Spec`), so it preserves the δ cofiltered limit. -/
   172	noncomputable instance : PreservesLimitsOfShape (FinSubext k K)ᵒᵖ Scheme.Spec.{u} :=
   173	  inferInstance
   174	
   175	omit [Algebra.IsAlgebraic k K] in
   176	/-- **The δ bridge (definitional).**  Forgetting the base of the δ *scheme* diagram gives the
   177	δ *ring* diagram, opposite, under `Scheme.Spec`: both send `k'' ↦ Spec k''`. -/
   178	lemma deltaScheme_forget_eq :
   179	    deltaSchemeDiagram (k := k) (K := K) ⋙ Over.forget (Spec (.of k))
   180	      = deltaRingDiagram.op ⋙ Scheme.Spec := rfl
   181	
   182	/-- The forgotten δ scheme diagram (`k'' ↦ Spec k''` in `Scheme`) has a limit `Spec K`: it is
   183	`Scheme.Spec` of the δ ring colimit `deltaIsColimit` (opposite), and `Scheme.Spec` (right adjoint
   184	`Γ ⊣ Spec`) preserves limits.  This is the honest `Spec K_s = lim_{k''} Spec k''`. -/
   185	noncomputable instance hasLimit_deltaScheme_forget :
   186	    HasLimit (deltaSchemeDiagram (k := k) (K := K) ⋙ Over.forget (Spec (.of k))) := by
   187	  rw [deltaScheme_forget_eq]
   188	  exact ⟨_, isLimitOfPreserves Scheme.Spec deltaIsColimit.op⟩
   189	
   190	/-- **The δ scheme colimit `Spec K = lim S`.**  The δ scheme diagram `S` has a limit — `Spec K`:
   191	`Over.forget (Spec k)` *creates* limits of this (cofiltered ⟹ connected) shape, lifting the
   192	forgotten limit `Spec K = Scheme.Spec (colim_{k''} k'')` (`hasLimit_deltaScheme_forget`) uniquely
   193	to `Over (Spec k)`.  So the δ scheme system `S` is a legal input to the β1 residual
   194	`Pic0PreservesFilteredBaseColimit`, and its limit is `Spec K_s`. -/
   195	noncomputable instance : HasLimit (deltaSchemeDiagram (k := k) (K := K)) := by
   196	  haveI : IsConnected (FinSubext k K)ᵒᵖ := IsCofiltered.isConnected _
   197	  exact hasLimit_of_created (deltaSchemeDiagram (k := k) (K := K)) (Over.forget (Spec (.of k)))
   198	
   199	end SchemeLimit

   201	/-! ## The δ system plugs into the β1 residual, and the mountain
   202	
   203	`preservesColimit_deltaScheme_of_residual` closes the loop of deliverable 1: the concrete δ
   204	scheme system `deltaSchemeDiagram` (all its residual hypotheses — affine transition maps,
   205	compact and quasi-separated stages, `HasLimit`/`Spec K = lim S` — discharged above) **is a legal
   206	input** to the β1 residual `Pic0PreservesFilteredBaseColimit C`, and feeding it in yields the
   207	concrete β1-at-`K_s` statement:

   210	> i.e. `colim_{k''} pic0Subgroup C (Spec k'') → pic0Subgroup C (Spec K_s)` is a bijection.

   232	
   233	variable {k : Type u} [Field k] (C : Over (Spec (.of k)))
   234	  [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom] [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom]
   235	variable (K : Type u) [Field K] [Algebra k K] [Algebra.IsAlgebraic k K]

   238	`Pic0PreservesFilteredBaseColimit C` (the pinned M–L mountain), the concrete δ scheme system
   239	`deltaSchemeDiagram`, with all its residual hypotheses discharged (affine transition maps,
   240	compact and quasi-separated `Spec`-of-field stages, and `HasLimit`/`Spec K = lim S`), yields

   242	`colim_{k''} pic0(Spec k'') → pic0(Spec K)`.  This is the honest consumption of the δ substrate
   243	by the residual, `divRep`-free. -/
   244	theorem preservesColimit_deltaScheme_of_residual
   245	    (h : Pic0PreservesFilteredBaseColimit C) :

     9	/-!
    10	# DAT-G0 β1 — the base-field directed system `K_s = colim k''` (DG-G0.δ) and the pinned residual
    11	
    12	This file lands **DG-G0.δ** (mini-spec `informal/spec-datg0.md` §3, landing notes I-0259/I-0263):
    13	the base-field directed system whose colimit is the separable closure `K_s`, over which the
    14	β1 residual `Pic0PreservesFilteredBaseColimit` (landed in `Picard/PicRepColimitCompat.lean`,
    15	commit c9df8d479) is quantified.
    16	
    17	## DG-G0.δ — the substrate the residual quantifies over
    18	
    19	For a **separable algebraic** extension `K/k` (the case `K = K_s` a separable closure is the
    20	DAT-G0 target), the finite subextensions form a **directed system** whose supremum is all of
    21	`K`.  Concretely:
    22	
    23	* `FinSubext k K` — the index: finite(-dimensional) `k`-subextensions `k''` of `K`, ordered by
    24	  inclusion.  It is **nonempty** and **directed** (`instNonemptyFinSubext`,
    25	  `directed_finSubext`), so `(FinSubext k K)ᵒᵖ` is `IsCofiltered` — the shape the residual's
    26	  `[IsCofiltered J]` binder consumes.
    27	* `iSup_finSubext_eq_top` — `⨆ k'', k'' = ⊤`, i.e. **`K = colim k''`** at the lattice level.
    28	* `coe_iSup_finSubext` — the colimit-is-**union** identity `↑(⨆ k'', k'') = ⋃ k'', ↑k''`
    29	  (`IntermediateField.coe_iSup_of_directed`): every element of `K` already lives at a finite
    30	  stage.  This is the honest content of "`K_s = colim k''`": the test-scheme limit
    31	  `S_{K_s} = lim S_{k''}` is `Spec` of this filtered colimit of fields.
    32	* `isSeparable_finSubext` — every stage `k''/k` is **separable** (`Algebra.IsSeparable`,
    33	  inherited from `K/k` by `Algebra.isSeparable_tower_bot_of_isSeparable`); with
    34	  `IntermediateField.isSeparable_iSup` the colimit is separable, so this is genuinely the
    35	  system of *finite separable* subextensions of `K_s/k`.
    36	
    37	All native `k`-algebra / scalar-tower instances come from the `IntermediateField` API
    38	(`Algebra k k''`, `IsScalarTower k k'' K`), per the I-0255 tower-diamond wall — no composite
    39	`RingHom.toAlgebra` `letI`s are built here.
    40	
    41	## The β1 residual (pinned — `Pic0PreservesFilteredBaseColimit`, in `PicRepColimitCompat`)
    42	
    43	The β1 reduction is LANDED (`PicRepColimitCompat.lean`, c9df8d479): the base-field-change
    44	functoriality of `pic0` is the landed natural iso `pic0ThetaType`, collapsing the varying-field
    45	colimit onto the single fixed functor `pic0TypeFunctor C` over `k`, whose base-field-colimit
    46	compatibility is the named `Prop`
    47	
    48	```
    49	Pic0PreservesFilteredBaseColimit C :=
    50	  ∀ ⦃J⦄ [SmallCategory J] [IsCofiltered J] (S : J ⥤ Over (Spec (.of k))),
    51	    (∀ f, IsAffineHom (S.map f).left) → (∀ i, CompactSpace (S.obj i).left) →
    52	    (∀ i, QuasiSeparatedSpace (S.obj i).left) → ∀ [HasLimit S],
    53	      PreservesColimit S.op (pic0TypeFunctor C)
    54	```
    55	
    56	`instConsumesFiniteBaseColimit` below records that this `Prop` **applies to** the δ system:
    57	`(FinSubext k K)ᵒᵖ` is `IsCofiltered`, so any cofiltered diagram `S` of test schemes indexed by
    58	it (in particular the `Spec`-of-tests limit `S_{K_s} = lim_{k''} S_{k''}`) is a legal input.
    59	
    60	**The residual proper is NOT discharged here** — it is genuinely M–L (I-0263): it says
    61	`pic0TypeFunctor C` is *locally of finite presentation as a functor*, which on affine tests
    62	`overSpec k A` is exactly that the affine relative-Picard construction `PicEtAff C A` commutes
    63	with filtered colimits of the test algebra `A`, riding finite presentation of the proper smooth
    64	curve `C/k`.  The precise remaining goal state and its named mathlib avatars
    65	(`CommRingCat.preservesColimit_coyoneda_of_finitePresentation`,
    66	`Scheme.exists_π_app_comp_eq_of_locallyOfFinitePresentation`, …) are pinned in the
    67	`PicRepColimitCompat` module docstring and landing note I-0263; this file lands the δ substrate
    68	they act on and leaves the analytic core `sorry`-free-pinned (no `sorry` in this file).
    69	-/

    79	/-! ## DG-G0.δ — the base-field directed system `K_s = colim k''` -/
    80	
    81	section FieldSystem
    82	
    83	variable (k K : Type u) [Field k] [Field K] [Algebra k K]
    84	
    85	/-- **The DG-G0.δ index** — the finite subextensions `k''` of a separable algebraic extension
    86	`K/k`, ordered by inclusion.  Its directed supremum is `K` (`iSup_finSubext_eq_top`); its
    87	opposite is the `IsCofiltered` shape the β1 residual `Pic0PreservesFilteredBaseColimit`
    88	quantifies over.  For `K = K_s` a separable closure these are exactly the *finite separable*
    89	subextensions of `K_s/k`. -/
    90	abbrev FinSubext : Type u := {L : IntermediateField k K // FiniteDimensional k L}
    91	
    92	variable {k K}
    93	
    94	/-- Each stage carries its finite-dimensionality as an instance. -/
    95	instance (L : FinSubext k K) : FiniteDimensional k L.1 := L.2
    96	
    97	variable (k K) in
    98	/-- The δ index is nonempty (`k` itself, as `⊥`, is a finite subextension). -/
    99	instance instNonemptyFinSubext [Algebra.IsAlgebraic k K] : Nonempty (FinSubext k K) :=
   100	  ⟨⟨k⟮(0 : K)⟯, adjoin.finiteDimensional (Algebra.IsIntegral.isIntegral _)⟩⟩
   101	
   102	/-- **DG-G0.δ, directedness.**  The finite subextensions of `K/k` are directed under inclusion:
   103	the join `k'' ⊔ k'''` of two finite subextensions is again finite.  Hence `(FinSubext k K)ᵒᵖ` is
   104	`IsCofiltered` — the shape the residual consumes. -/
   105	theorem directed_finSubext :
   106	    Directed (· ≤ ·) (fun L : FinSubext k K => (L.1 : IntermediateField k K)) := by
   107	  intro L₁ L₂
   108	  haveI := L₁.2
   109	  haveI := L₂.2
   110	  exact ⟨⟨L₁.1 ⊔ L₂.1, IntermediateField.finiteDimensional_sup _ _⟩, le_sup_left, le_sup_right⟩
   111	
   112	/-- **DG-G0.δ, `IsDirected`.**  The δ index is a directed order (from `directed_finSubext`), so it
   113	is `IsFiltered` and its opposite `(FinSubext k K)ᵒᵖ` is `IsCofiltered` — automatically, via
   114	`isFiltered_of_directed_le_nonempty` and `isCofiltered_op_of_isFiltered`. -/
   115	instance instIsDirectedFinSubext [Algebra.IsAlgebraic k K] :
   116	    IsDirected (FinSubext k K) (· ≤ ·) :=
   117	  ⟨fun L₁ L₂ => directed_finSubext L₁ L₂⟩
   118	
   119	/-- **DG-G0.δ, the cofiltered shape the residual consumes.**  `(FinSubext k K)ᵒᵖ` is
   120	`IsCofiltered` — exactly the `[IsCofiltered J]` shape of `Pic0PreservesFilteredBaseColimit`'s
   121	diagram binder.  A cofiltered diagram of test schemes `S : (FinSubext k K)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Over (Spec k)`
   122	indexed by it — in particular the `Spec`-of-tests limit `S_{K_s} = lim_{k''} S_{k''}` (with
   123	affine transition maps `Spec k''' → Spec k''` and one-point, hence compact and quasi-separated,
   124	stages) — is therefore a legal input to the β1 residual. -/
   125	instance instIsCofilteredFinSubextOp [Algebra.IsAlgebraic k K] :
   126	    IsCofiltered (FinSubext k K)ᵒᵖ :=
   127	  inferInstance
   128	
   129	/-- **DG-G0.δ, the colimit at the lattice level: `K = colim k''`.**  For an algebraic extension
   130	`K/k` the supremum of the finite subextensions is all of `K`: every `x : K` is algebraic, hence
   131	lies in the finite subextension `k⟮x⟯`. -/
   132	theorem iSup_finSubext_eq_top [Algebra.IsAlgebraic k K] :
   133	    ⨆ L : FinSubext k K, (L.1 : IntermediateField k K) = ⊤ :=
   134	  le_top.antisymm fun x _ =>
   135	    le_iSup (fun L : FinSubext k K => (L.1 : IntermediateField k K))
   136	      ⟨k⟮x⟯, adjoin.finiteDimensional (Algebra.IsIntegral.isIntegral x)⟩ <|
   137	      mem_adjoin_simple_self k x
   138	
   139	/-- **DG-G0.δ, colimit-is-union.**  The directed supremum of the finite subextensions is their
   140	set-theoretic **union** (`IntermediateField.coe_iSup_of_directed`): the honest "`K_s = colim k''`"
   141	statement.  Combined with `iSup_finSubext_eq_top`, every element of `K` already lives at a finite
   142	stage `k''`. -/
   143	theorem coe_iSup_finSubext [Algebra.IsAlgebraic k K] :
   144	    (↑(⨆ L : FinSubext k K, (L.1 : IntermediateField k K)) : Set K)
   145	      = ⋃ L : FinSubext k K, (L.1 : Set K) :=
   146	  IntermediateField.coe_iSup_of_directed directed_finSubext
   147	
   148	/-- **DG-G0.δ, separability of each stage.**  Every finite subextension `k''/k` of a separable
   149	extension `K/k` is itself separable (`Algebra.isSeparable_tower_bot_of_isSeparable` on the native
   150	tower `k → k'' → K`).  With `IntermediateField.isSeparable_iSup` the colimit `⨆ k''` is separable,
   151	so the δ system is the directed system of *finite separable* subextensions. -/
   152	instance isSeparable_finSubext [Algebra.IsSeparable k K] (L : FinSubext k K) :
   153	    Algebra.IsSeparable k L.1 :=
   154	  Algebra.isSeparable_tower_bot_of_isSeparable k L.1 K
   155	
   156	end FieldSystem

   158	end AlgebraicGeometry.DatG0

import AlgebraicJacobian.Descent.TensorProductPushoutBaseChange

/-!
# Maps through a tower of scalar extensions

This file isolates the elementary algebra behind finite-stage maps.  An algebra map can
be extended along a scalar map, and the cancellation equivalence for a tower identifies
that extension with any ambient map which commutes with the direct scalar extension.
-/

set_option autoImplicit false

open scoped TensorProduct

universe u

namespace AlgebraicJacobian

noncomputable section

/-- Scalar extension of an algebra map.  This is the map-level form of
`scalarExtensionMap`, whose special case induced by an algebra structure is recorded
separately in the pushout base-change file. -/
def scalarExtensionMapOfAlgHom {R K A B : Type u}
    [CommRing R] [CommRing K] [Semiring A] [Semiring B]
    [Algebra R K] [Algebra R A] [Algebra R B]
    (f : A →ₐ[R] B) :
    (K ⊗[R] A) →ₐ[K] (K ⊗[R] B) :=
  Algebra.TensorProduct.map (AlgHom.id K K) f

/-- `scalarExtensionMapOfAlgHom` sends a pure tensor by applying the original map to
its algebra factor. -/
@[simp]
theorem scalarExtensionMapOfAlgHom_tmul {R K A B : Type u}
    [CommRing R] [CommRing K] [Semiring A] [Semiring B]
    [Algebra R K] [Algebra R A] [Algebra R B]
    (f : A →ₐ[R] B) (c : K) (a : A) :
    scalarExtensionMapOfAlgHom (R := R) (K := K) f (c ⊗ₜ[R] a) =
      c ⊗ₜ[R] f a := by
  simp [scalarExtensionMapOfAlgHom]

/-- Scalar extension of a map is natural in a tower of scalar rings. -/
theorem scalarExtensionMapOfAlgHom_tower {F L K A B : Type u}
    [CommRing F] [CommRing L] [CommRing K] [Semiring A] [Semiring B]
    [Algebra F L] [Algebra F K] [Algebra L K] [IsScalarTower F L K]
    [Algebra F A] [Algebra F B]
    (f : A →ₐ[F] B) :
    (Algebra.TensorProduct.map (IsScalarTower.toAlgHom F L K)
        (AlgHom.id F B)).comp
        ((scalarExtensionMapOfAlgHom (R := F) (K := L) f).restrictScalars F) =
      ((scalarExtensionMapOfAlgHom (R := F) (K := K) f).restrictScalars F).comp
        (Algebra.TensorProduct.map (IsScalarTower.toAlgHom F L K)
          (AlgHom.id F A)) := by
  ext x
  · simp [scalarExtensionMapOfAlgHom]
  · simp [scalarExtensionMapOfAlgHom]

/-- Scalar extension preserves composition of algebra maps. -/
@[simp]
theorem scalarExtensionMapOfAlgHom_comp {R K A B D : Type u}
    [CommRing R] [CommRing K] [Semiring A] [Semiring B] [Semiring D]
    [Algebra R K] [Algebra R A] [Algebra R B] [Algebra R D]
    (f : A →ₐ[R] B) (g : B →ₐ[R] D) :
    (scalarExtensionMapOfAlgHom (R := R) (K := K) g).comp
        (scalarExtensionMapOfAlgHom (R := R) (K := K) f) =
      scalarExtensionMapOfAlgHom (R := R) (K := K) (g.comp f) := by
  ext x
  · simp [scalarExtensionMapOfAlgHom]

/-- Scalar extension preserves the identity algebra map. -/
@[simp]
theorem scalarExtensionMapOfAlgHom_id {R K A : Type u}
    [CommRing R] [CommRing K] [Semiring A]
    [Algebra R K] [Algebra R A] :
    scalarExtensionMapOfAlgHom (R := R) (K := K) (AlgHom.id R A) =
      AlgHom.id K (K ⊗[R] A) := by
  ext x
  · simp [scalarExtensionMapOfAlgHom]

/-- Cancellation on a tensor whose right factor is itself a scalar extension. -/
theorem cancelBaseChange_tmul_baseChange {F L K A : Type u}
    [CommRing F] [CommRing L] [CommRing K] [CommRing A]
    [Algebra F L] [Algebra F K] [Algebra L K] [IsScalarTower F L K]
    [Algebra F A] (c : K) (x : L ⊗[F] A) :
    Algebra.TensorProduct.cancelBaseChange F L K K A (c ⊗ₜ[L] x) =
      c • Algebra.TensorProduct.map
        (IsScalarTower.toAlgHom F L K) (AlgHom.id F A) x := by
  induction x using TensorProduct.induction_on with
  | zero => simp
  | add x y hx hy =>
      rw [TensorProduct.tmul_add, map_add, hx, hy, map_add, smul_add]
  | tmul l a =>
      simp [Algebra.TensorProduct.cancelBaseChange_tmul, Algebra.smul_def, mul_comm]

/-- Cancellation is natural for maps between two base changes from `F` to `L` which
commute with their direct scalar extensions from `L` to `K`. -/
theorem cancelBaseChange_naturality {F L K A B : Type u}
    [CommRing F] [CommRing L] [CommRing K] [CommRing A] [CommRing B]
    [Algebra F L] [Algebra F K] [Algebra L K] [IsScalarTower F L K]
    [Algebra F A] [Algebra F B]
    (phiL : L ⊗[F] A →ₐ[L] L ⊗[F] B)
    (phiK : K ⊗[F] A →ₐ[K] K ⊗[F] B)
    (hphi :
      (Algebra.TensorProduct.map (IsScalarTower.toAlgHom F L K) (AlgHom.id F B)).comp
          (phiL.restrictScalars F) =
        (phiK.restrictScalars F).comp
          (Algebra.TensorProduct.map (IsScalarTower.toAlgHom F L K) (AlgHom.id F A))) :
    (Algebra.TensorProduct.cancelBaseChange F L K K B).toAlgHom.comp
        (scalarExtensionMapOfAlgHom (R := L) (K := K) phiL) =
      phiK.comp (Algebra.TensorProduct.cancelBaseChange F L K K A).toAlgHom := by
  apply DFunLike.ext _ _
  intro x
  induction x using TensorProduct.induction_on with
  | zero => simp
  | add x y hx hy => simp [map_add, hx, hy]
  | tmul c x =>
      change Algebra.TensorProduct.cancelBaseChange F L K K B
          (scalarExtensionMapOfAlgHom (R := L) (K := K) phiL (c ⊗ₜ[L] x)) =
        phiK (Algebra.TensorProduct.cancelBaseChange F L K K A (c ⊗ₜ[L] x))
      rw [scalarExtensionMapOfAlgHom_tmul, cancelBaseChange_tmul_baseChange,
        cancelBaseChange_tmul_baseChange]
      rw [show phiK (c • (Algebra.TensorProduct.map
          (IsScalarTower.toAlgHom F L K) (AlgHom.id F A)) x) =
          c • phiK ((Algebra.TensorProduct.map
            (IsScalarTower.toAlgHom F L K) (AlgHom.id F A)) x) from
        phiK.toLinearMap.map_smul c _]
      have h := DFunLike.congr_fun hphi x
      change
        (Algebra.TensorProduct.map (IsScalarTower.toAlgHom F L K) (AlgHom.id F B))
            (phiL x) =
          phiK ((Algebra.TensorProduct.map (IsScalarTower.toAlgHom F L K)
            (AlgHom.id F A)) x) at h
      exact congrArg (fun z => c • z) h

end

/-- The scalar-extension tower square, with the ambient map written using the
canonical value map of a finite subextension. -/
theorem scalarExtensionMapOfAlgHom_tower_finSubext
    {F K A B : Type u}
    [Field F] [Field K] [Algebra F K] [Algebra.IsAlgebraic F K]
    [Semiring A] [Algebra F A] [Semiring B] [Algebra F B]
    (N : DatG0.FinSubext F K) (f : A →ₐ[F] B) :
    (Algebra.TensorProduct.map N.1.val (AlgHom.id F B)).comp
        ((AlgebraicJacobian.scalarExtensionMapOfAlgHom
          (R := F) (K := N.1) f).restrictScalars F) =
      ((AlgebraicJacobian.scalarExtensionMapOfAlgHom
        (R := F) (K := K) f).restrictScalars F).comp
        (Algebra.TensorProduct.map N.1.val (AlgHom.id F A)) := by
  have hval : N.1.val = IsScalarTower.toAlgHom F N.1 K := by
    ext x
    rfl
  have htower := AlgebraicJacobian.scalarExtensionMapOfAlgHom_tower
    (F := F) (L := N.1) (K := K) f
  rw [← hval] at htower
  exact htower

/-! ## One finite family containing charts and overlaps -/

/-- A finite tag for every chart ring and every ordered pair-overlap ring in the atlas. -/
abbrev Pic0FiniteStageRingIndex :=
  Pic0FiniteStageChartIndex C ⊕
    (Pic0FiniteStageChartIndex C × Pic0FiniteStageChartIndex C)

/-- The ring selected by a finite-stage ring tag. -/
def Pic0FiniteStageRing (i : Pic0FiniteStageRingIndex C) : Type u :=
  match i with
  | Sum.inl U => Pic0FiniteStageChartRing C U
  | Sum.inr UV => Pic0FiniteStageOverlapRing C UV.1 UV.2

instance (i : Pic0FiniteStageRingIndex C) :
    CommRing (Pic0FiniteStageRing C i) := by
  rcases i with U | ⟨U, V⟩
  · change CommRing (Pic0FiniteStageChartRing C U)
    infer_instance
  · change CommRing (Pic0FiniteStageOverlapRing C U V)
    infer_instance

noncomputable instance (i : Pic0FiniteStageRingIndex C) :
    Algebra k (Pic0FiniteStageRing C i) := by
  rcases i with U | ⟨U, V⟩
  · change Algebra k (Pic0FiniteStageChartRing C U)
    infer_instance
  · change Algebra k (Pic0FiniteStageOverlapRing C U V)
    infer_instance

/-- Every ring in the combined finite family is finitely presented over the ground field. -/
theorem finitePresentation_pic0FiniteStageRing
    (i : Pic0FiniteStageRingIndex C) :
    Algebra.FinitePresentation k (Pic0FiniteStageRing C i) := by
  rcases i with U | ⟨U, V⟩
  · exact finitePresentation_pic0FiniteStageChartRing C U
  · exact finitePresentation_pic0FiniteStageOverlapRing C U V
    letI : Algebra (K ⊗[R] A) (K ⊗[R] B₁) := g₁.toRingHom.toAlgebra
    letI : Algebra (K ⊗[R] A) (K ⊗[R] B₂) := g₂.toRingHom.toAlgebra

     8	/-!
     9	# Pair-transition maps in the finite-stage Picard atlas
    10	
    11	The ordered overlaps `U ∩ V` and `V ∩ U` in the exact separably closed Picard atlas are
    12	canonically identified by restriction along `inf_comm`.  This file adds those transition
    13	maps to the already descended restriction legs and spreads the entire finite family out over
    14	one common finite subextension.  At that stage the restriction legs are open immersions and
    15	the two transition directions are inverse.
    16	
    17	This is not yet a `Scheme.GlueData`.  Its triple-overlap objects are pullbacks of restriction
    18	legs, and constructing their `t'` maps and cyclic cocycle is the next boundary.
    19	-/
    20	
    21	set_option autoImplicit false
    22	
    23	universe u
    24	
    25	open CategoryTheory Limits TopologicalSpace TensorProduct

    32	variable {k : Type u} [Field k] (C : Over (Spec (.of k)))

    36	/-! ## Exact pair transitions -/
    37	
    38	/-- The finite family of ordered pairs indexing overlap-transition maps. -/
    39	abbrev Pic0FiniteStageTransitionIndex :=
    40	  Pic0FiniteStageChartIndex C × Pic0FiniteStageChartIndex C
    41	
    42	/-- The source ring of the transition indexed by `(U, V)` is the reversed overlap ring. -/
    43	def Pic0FiniteStageTransitionSource (p : Pic0FiniteStageTransitionIndex C) :
    44	    Pic0FiniteStageRingIndex C :=
    45	  Sum.inr (p.2, p.1)
    46	
    47	/-- The target ring of the transition indexed by `(U, V)` is the forward overlap ring. -/
    48	def Pic0FiniteStageTransitionTarget (p : Pic0FiniteStageTransitionIndex C) :
    49	    Pic0FiniteStageRingIndex C :=
    50	  Sum.inr p
    51	
    52	/-- The algebra map underlying the canonical transition from the reversed ordered overlap
    53	to the forward ordered overlap.  On schemes, `Spec.map` reverses this direction. -/
    54	noncomputable def pic0FiniteStageTransition
    55	    (p : Pic0FiniteStageTransitionIndex C) :
    56	    Pic0FiniteStageRing C (Pic0FiniteStageTransitionSource C p) →ₐ[k]
    57	      Pic0FiniteStageRing C (Pic0FiniteStageTransitionTarget C p) := by
    58	  rcases p with ⟨U, V⟩
    59	  let J := (pic0_sepClosed_representableBy (C := C)).1
    60	  letI : J.left.Over (Spec (.of k)) := ⟨J.hom⟩
    61	  have hUVVU : U.1.1 ⊓ V.1.1 ≤ V.1.1 ⊓ U.1.1 := by
    62	    rw [inf_comm]
    63	  exact
    64	    { J.left.resHom hUVVU with
    65	      commutes' := fun r =>
    66	        J.left.overAlgebraMap_apply_res k (homOfLE hUVVU).op r }
    67	
    68	/-- Reversing an exact pair transition gives its inverse. -/
    69	theorem pic0FiniteStageTransition_inverse
    70	    (U V : Pic0FiniteStageChartIndex C) :
    71	    (pic0FiniteStageTransition C (V, U)).comp
    72	        (pic0FiniteStageTransition C (U, V)) =
    73	      AlgHom.id k (Pic0FiniteStageOverlapRing C V U) := by
    74	  apply DFunLike.ext _ _
    75	  intro x
    76	  change
    77	    ((pic0_sepClosed_representableBy (C := C)).1.left.resHom
    78	      (show V.1.1 ⊓ U.1.1 ≤ U.1.1 ⊓ V.1.1 by rw [inf_comm]))
    79	      (((pic0_sepClosed_representableBy (C := C)).1.left.resHom
    80	        (show U.1.1 ⊓ V.1.1 ≤ V.1.1 ⊓ U.1.1 by rw [inf_comm])) x) = x
    81	  rw [Scheme.resHom_resHom, Scheme.resHom_self]

    84	
    85	/-- A finite index type containing every restriction leg and every pair transition. -/
    86	abbrev Pic0FiniteStageMapIndex :=

    88	
    89	/-- Source-ring tag for the combined finite family. -/
    90	def Pic0FiniteStageMapSource :
    91	    Pic0FiniteStageMapIndex C → Pic0FiniteStageRingIndex C
    92	  | Sum.inl i => Pic0FiniteStageRestrictionSource C i
    93	  | Sum.inr p => Pic0FiniteStageTransitionSource C p
    94	
    95	/-- Target-ring tag for the combined finite family. -/
    96	def Pic0FiniteStageMapTarget :
    97	    Pic0FiniteStageMapIndex C → Pic0FiniteStageRingIndex C
    98	  | Sum.inl i => Pic0FiniteStageRestrictionTarget C i
    99	  | Sum.inr p => Pic0FiniteStageTransitionTarget C p

   101	/-- The exact combined family: restrictions on the left summand and pair transitions on the

   107	  rcases q with i | p
   108	  · exact pic0FiniteStageRestriction C i
   109	  · exact pic0FiniteStageTransition C p

   149	-- The source and target quotient algebras depend on the ordered chart pair.
   150	/-- The transported ambient transitions in opposite directions are inverse. -/
   151	theorem pic0FiniteStageTransportedTransition_inverse
   152	    {F : Type u} [Field F] [Algebra F k]
   153	    (L : DatG0.FinSubext F k)
   154	    (n m : Pic0FiniteStageRingIndex C → ℕ)
   155	    (relation : ∀ j, Fin (m j) → MvPolynomial (Fin (n j)) L.1)
   156	    (e : ∀ j,
   157	      k ⊗[L.1] DatG0.FiniteRelationAlgebra L.1 (n j) (m j) (relation j) ≃ₐ[k]
   158	        Pic0FiniteStageRing C j)
   159	    (U V : Pic0FiniteStageChartIndex C) :
   160	    (pic0FiniteStageTransportedMap C L n m relation e (Sum.inr (V, U))).comp
   161	        (pic0FiniteStageTransportedMap C L n m relation e (Sum.inr (U, V))) =
   162	      AlgHom.id k

   192	-- The conclusion contains one dependent quotient-algebra instance for every finite tag.
   193	set_option maxHeartbeats 1600000 in
   194	-- The simultaneous descent and equation reflection require a larger elaboration budget.
   195	/-- All exact restriction and pair-transition maps have simultaneous models over one finite

   197	are inverse at that same finite stage. -/
   198	theorem exists_finSubext_pic0FiniteStageTransition_models
   199	    {F : Type u} [Field F] [Algebra F k] [Algebra.IsAlgebraic F k] :

   224	                  (DatG0.FiniteRelationAlgebra L.1
   225	                    (n (Pic0FiniteStageMapSource C q))
   226	                    (m (Pic0FiniteStageMapSource C q))
   227	                    (relation (Pic0FiniteStageMapSource C q)))))) ∧
   228	        (∀ i : Pic0FiniteStageRestrictionIndex C,
   229	          IsOpenImmersion
   230	            (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (mapM (Sum.inl i)).toRingHom))) ∧
   231	        (∀ U V : Pic0FiniteStageChartIndex C,
   232	          (mapM (Sum.inr (V, U))).comp (mapM (Sum.inr (U, V))) =
   233	            AlgHom.id M.1
   234	              (Pic0FiniteStageModelRing C L n m relation M (Sum.inr (V, U)))) := by

   237	    exists_finSubext_pic0FiniteStageRestriction_openImmersion_models
   238	      (C := C) (F := F)

   244	          (n (Pic0FiniteStageMapSource C q))
   245	          (m (Pic0FiniteStageMapSource C q))
   246	          (relation (Pic0FiniteStageMapSource C q)))

   249	          (n (Pic0FiniteStageMapTarget C q))
   250	          (m (Pic0FiniteStageMapTarget C q))
   251	          (relation (Pic0FiniteStageMapTarget C q)))
